proves: PINNED DEFECT. A z-index:-1 child is never hoisted out of a parent that establishes no stacking context, so every node here behaves as though it established one.
checkable: 200x72, three 56x56 red cells at y=8..63, each holding a 36x36 blue child at z-index -1 inset 10,10. Sample the child's centre at y=35: cell 0 at x=35, cell 1 at x=99, cell 2 at x=163. Today cells 0 and 1 read 40,80,220 and cell 2 reads 42,82,220 - the same 0.99 opacity that lifts its parent's red. Cells 0 and 1 must read 220,40,40 once the painter hoists; cell 2 must still read 42,82,220, unchanged. The parent's own red reads 220,40,40 at x=12 and 220,42,42 at x=140, the second being the 0.99 opacity.
expected: cell 0 is a plain parent and cell 1 clips with overflow:hidden. Neither establishes a stacking context, so the child belongs to the grandparent and paints before the parent's background - Chrome hides it in both, measured with elementFromPoint. Cell 2's parent has opacity 0.99, which does establish one, so its child belongs to it and paints above its background: that cell is correct today and is the control.
why_three: two cells flipping while one holds says the fix was the hoist rather than a change of sign. A fixture with only the two defective cells would pass if the painter started hiding every negative child.
clipping: cell 1 also guards a property this renderer has by construction: enter_node clips with clip_to_box rather than opening a layer, so overflow:hidden creates no context. It is the trigger most often assumed to create one. A change that reaches for save_layer to clip would establish a context the Chrome measurement says must not exist, and this cell's picture would move.
status: measured from the committed image, and against Chrome. Accept again when the painter is fixed; the first two cells are expected to move and the third is not.
